email.subject: Just moved to 18 Tamarind Way - lots of questions!
email.body:
Hi there! We just closed on 18 Tamarind Way last Thursday and moved in over the weekend. A few questions, sorry for the long list:

1. How do we register to vote at the new address? We were registered in Harlow County before.
2. We have a beagle, Pepper, licensed in Harlow. Do we need a new dog license here or does that one transfer?
3. Our son starts 4th grade next week. Which school is he zoned for and how do we enroll?
4. Water: the seller told us they'd be closing their water account on Friday. We haven't set anything up in our name yet. Will the water just keep running, or will it get shut off? We have a newborn so we really can't be without water.
5. I think our street has those permit-parking signs? Our second car has been parked on the street since Saturday. Do we need a permit?

Thanks so much, Adaeze Okafor, 555-0193

routing_rules.RR-1: Emails with several unrelated requests go to the Resident Services Desk, which answers all items and opens tickets as needed.
routing_rules.RR-2: EXCEPTION: if any single request concerns a service that is about to be shut off, a safety hazard, or a legal deadline the writer mentions, route the email to the department that owns that request, and copy Resident Services for the remaining items.
routing_rules.RR-3: School enrollment belongs to the independent school district; answer with a referral.

department_notes.Water Customer Service: Starts, stops and transfers water accounts. When a seller closes an account at a sale, the meter is locked shortly afterwards unless a new owner has applied. New-owner applications can be taken by phone the same day.
department_notes.Parking Services: Residential permit zones are posted with green-and-white signs; vehicles without permits may be ticketed after 72 hours.
department_notes.Animal Services: Dog licenses are issued by the city; licenses from other jurisdictions do not transfer.
department_notes.Elections Office: Voter registration updates for new residents; moving from another county requires a new registration.
department_notes.Resident Services Desk: General questions and multi-issue emails; target reply within two business days.

state.welcome_packet_note: New homeowners receive a welcome packet from the Assessor about 6 weeks after closing, with trash pickup days, recycling rules and the property tax calendar.

state: PROGRAM RULES - Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program (SFMNP), 2026 season. R-1: Eligible applicants are (a) aged 60 or older by the end of the season, or (b) aged 55-59 with a disability and living in a senior housing facility that participates in the program. R-2: Household income must be at or below 185% of the federal poverty guideline, as certified by the eligibility system (field income_cert). R-3: One benefit per household per season; if two eligible people live together, only one set of vouchers is issued. R-4: Proxies may pick up vouchers with a signed proxy form. R-5: Vouchers are valid at participating farm stands through October 31. R-6: Benefits are issued first come, first served until the county allocation is exhausted; waitlisted applicants are served if vouchers are returned. R-7: A household that disagrees with a decision may ask for a supervisor review within the season. R-8: Lost vouchers are not replaced.

APPLICATION SF-26-0418 (received 2026-06-03): Applicant Lorenzo Bianchi, age 58. Address: Maple Court Senior Apartments, Unit 212. Disability: 'Yes - receives SSDI (Parkinson's)'. Household: applicant and spouse Teresa Bianchi, age 61. Household income: SSDI plus the spouse's part-time pension. income_cert: 'At or below 185% - CERTIFIED'. Proxy: none. Notes from applicant: 'My wife already has her own card from the Eastside clinic, I'd like my own too because we shop separately. The market at Riverside Park is closest for me, I use a walker.'

FACILITY LIST (participating senior housing, 2026): Linden Terrace; Riverside Commons; Oak Hollow Manor. Maple Court Senior Apartments withdrew from the program on 2026-04-15 (staffing). Maple Court residents were told by letter in April that on-site voucher distribution would end.

PARTICIPATING FARM STANDS (2026): Riverside Park Saturday Market (8:00-13:00, May-October); Eastside Clinic Farm Stand (Wednesdays 10:00-14:00); Hollow Creek Orchard stand; Downtown Plaza Market (Thursdays).
WORKER NOTE 2026-06-05: Checked SFMNP issuance log: Teresa Bianchi, same address, vouchers issued 2026-05-28 at Eastside clinic. County allocation: 88% issued as of today.

WORKER NOTE 2026-06-06: Supervisor: under R-1(b), the facility must participate in the current season; check whether applicant qualifies any other way before denying. Disability documentation for R-1(b) has not been requested because the facility condition fails anyway.
WORKER NOTE 2026-06-07: Applicant called back; says his wife doesn't mind sharing her vouchers but he'd like his own for convenience.

request.text: I request the autopsy report, toxicology results and autopsy photographs for Daniel Voss, who died March 22, 2026 after a crash on Route 40. I understand there may be a criminal case against the other driver.

me_records_law.§4.1: Autopsy reports and toxicology results are public records.
me_records_law.§4.2: Autopsy photographs, video and audio are confidential and may be released only to the next of kin or by court order.
me_records_law.§4.3: While a criminal prosecution arising from the death is pending, the prosecutor may certify that release of the report or toxicology would interfere with the prosecution; certified records are withheld until the prosecution ends.
me_records_law.§4.4: A next-of-kin objection does not make a public record confidential, but the office must notify the next of kin before release.
me_records_law.§4.5: Personal identifiers of third parties (e.g., witnesses named in the investigator's narrative) are redacted.
me_records_law.§4.6: Records are released electronically; copying fees apply only to paper copies.

case_file.investigator_narrative: Includes names and phone numbers of two witnesses who stopped at the scene.

state.office_procedure: Next-of-kin notices are sent by certified mail and logged in the case file under 'NOK notice'. The office waits 5 business days after notice before releasing records. Photographs have been released to next of kin on request only; none have been requested in this case.
state.nok_contact: Next of kin on file: Ilse Voss (sister), 12 Lindenhof Rd.

correspondence.text: Certification under §4.3: release of toxicology in the Voss matter would interfere with the pending vehicular homicide prosecution of R. Keller. Autopsy report may be released.
Our family objects to any release. Please do not give reporters anything about my brother.
Autopsy report released to requester with witness identifiers redacted; toxicology withheld under §4.3 certification; photographs withheld under §4.2.
Update: R. Keller pleaded guilty on 07/28; sentencing set for September. The §4.3 certification is withdrawn as of today.
Now that the case is resolved, please send the toxicology results, and let me know whether the photographs can be released too.

The bar may have lifted but the record leaves real doubt
No bar applies; release after notifying next of kin
No bar and no notice step

still_pending.instructions: After the guilty plea, is the prosecution still 'pending' in the sense used by §4.3?

objection_effect.instructions: Under §4.4, what effect does the sister's objection have on the autopsy report?

criteria.notice_only: It only triggers notice before release

nok_notified.instructions: Does `state` show a next-of-kin notice logged for the toxicology release?

prosecution_status.instructions: What does the 2026-07-30 `correspondence` entry say about the prosecution?

photos.note: §4.2: photographs are confidential except to next of kin or by court order; the requester is a reporter.

toxicology_now.note: The DA withdrew the §4.3 certification on 07-30 after the plea, so no bar remains and §4.4 notice applies; but sentencing is still pending, and some reviewers would read 'prosecution pending' as continuing until sentencing.

still_pending.note: A plea with sentencing set for September means the case isn't fully concluded, but the DA withdrew the certification, suggesting interference is no longer a concern; reviewers split on the meaning of 'pending'.

objection_effect.note: §4.4: an objection does not make a public record confidential; it triggers notice.

tree_ordinance.T-2 Protected trees: Oaks, sycamores and bay laurels with a trunk diameter of 12 inches or more at 4.5 ft above grade, and any tree of 24 inches or more, are protected.
tree_ordinance.T-3 Permit: Removing a protected tree requires a tree removal permit and replacement planting at a 2:1 ratio or an in-lieu fee.
tree_ordinance.T-4 Hazard exception: A protected tree that is dead, dying or an imminent hazard may be removed with a hazard removal permit. The application must include a report from an ISA Certified Arborist stating the condition and the risk rating. Replacement planting is waived for dead trees but not for living hazard trees.
tree_ordinance.T-5 Emergency: If a tree poses an immediate threat to life or structures, it may be removed first, and the permit filed within 3 business days with photos and the arborist report.
tree_ordinance.T-6 Heritage trees: Trees listed on the Heritage Register need City Council approval regardless of condition.
tree_ordinance.T-7 In-lieu fee: The in-lieu fee is set per inch of trunk diameter removed and funds street-tree planting.

Subject: My rent went up - tenant ID LHA-30581

Dear Rent Calculation Unit,

I received my annual recertification letter dated April 10 saying my share of rent is going from $286 to $412 starting June 1. I have a few things to say.

First, I think the new amount is wrong. The letter says you counted $480 a month from 'unearned income - contributions'. That is money my brother sends sometimes to help with my medicine, it is not every month and it is not income, it is for my prescriptions. Some months he sends nothing. I would like the rent recalculated without it. I also receive SNAP, and my SNAP worker already knows about my brother's help and did not count it.

Second, as you know I use a wheelchair since my stroke. The recertification interview was held on the third floor of your office and the elevator was out of service. There was a sign saying it would be fixed 'next week', and it was the same sign when I came back two weeks later. I had to do the interview on the phone in the lobby with no privacy, with other people sitting right there listening to my income and my medical information. I would like my future appointments to be at a location I can get to, or by home visit.

Third, I also have medical expenses (prescriptions, the wheelchair repair) that I did not know I could report. I am attaching receipts from the last 12 months. I understand these can be deducted for disabled households. My neighbor in 4B told me she gets a deduction like this every year.

I have lived at Harbor Terrace for nine years and always reported everything. I don't understand why this year is different. My caseworker, Ms. Albright, retired in January and I have not been assigned a new one; nobody answers the number on the letter. The letter also says the rent will be recalculated if I report changes, but I never got the worksheet showing how you did the calculation. Could you send it? My sister Mariam helps me read these letters and can call you if you give me a name.

If you cannot fix this, please tell me how to ask for a hearing.

Thank you,
Yusuf Haddad
555-0158

deferral_ordinance.PTD-1 Eligibility: Owner-occupants may defer property taxes on their principal residence if (a) the owner is 65 or older or permanently disabled, and (b) household income is at or below the limit certified by the Treasurer (field income_cert).
